ai.definition: AI in Materials Science involves using machine learning and data-driven approaches to predict, design, and optimize material properties and structures.
ai.howItWorks: Machine learning algorithms are trained on large datasets containing information about various materials. These models can then be used to predict the properties of new or existing compounds without the need for extensive physical experiments.
ai.problemSolved: Accelerating the discovery and development of advanced materials by reducing the time and resources required for traditional trial-and-error methods.
ai.manufacturing: AI-driven predictive modeling can streamline the manufacturing process by optimizing conditions, reducing waste, and improving product quality.
ai.buildProcess: Data collection (experimental data, literature), model training using machine learning algorithms, validation through experimental testing, and integration into design workflows.
ai.costDrivers: Cost of data collection, computational resources for model training, and expertise in both AI and materials science.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: expected to grow as more companies adopt AI-driven approaches and the technology matures.
ai.regulation: Current regulatory frameworks are not yet fully adapted to the integration of AI in materials development, leading to potential gaps in oversight.
ai.risks: Data quality issues, model bias, intellectual property concerns, and the need for robust validation processes.
ai.profitability: Potential for significant cost savings and innovation-driven revenue growth, but current market is still nascent.
ai.futureDevelopment: Integration with other technologies like quantum computing to enhance predictive accuracy and explore new material properties.

glossary.def: A subset of artificial intelligence that involves training algorithms on data to make predictions or decisions without being explicitly programmed.
Methods that rely on analyzing and learning from large datasets to inform decision-making processes.

subsystems.name: Data infrastructure
subsystems.role: collects, cleans and standardises materials data so models can learn from it.

subsystems.name: Materials representation
subsystems.role: encodes composition and crystal structure into numbers or graphs that algorithms can process.

subsystems.name: Machine learning models
subsystems.role: predict properties and propose new candidate materials.
parts: generative models (e.g. variational autoencoders, diffusion models)

subsystems.name: Simulation engines
subsystems.role: generate training data and validate candidates before synthesis.

subsystems.name: Autonomous experimentation
subsystems.role: synthesises and tests candidates automatically, feeding results back to the models.

subsystems.name: Integration platform
subsystems.role: ties data, models, simulation and experiments into a closed loop.
parts: version control for models and data

buildSteps.title: Assemble data
buildSteps.detail: Gather experimental measurements and computed properties from literature and simulations into a consistent, machine-readable database.

buildSteps.title: Encode materials
buildSteps.detail: Convert chemical compositions and crystal structures into numerical features or graphs that preserve the geometry and bonding of the material.

buildSteps.title: Train predictive models
buildSteps.detail: Fit machine learning models to map the encoded material to target properties such as band gap, hardness or catalytic activity.

buildSteps.title: Screen large libraries
buildSteps.detail: Apply the trained models to millions of hypothetical or known-but-untested compounds to rank candidates by predicted performance.

buildSteps.title: Generate novel candidates
buildSteps.detail: Use generative models to propose entirely new structures that satisfy desired property targets, rather than only screening existing ones.

buildSteps.title: Validate in silico
buildSteps.detail: Run more accurate but slower simulations such as density functional theory or molecular dynamics to check stability and confirm predicted properties.

buildSteps.title: Synthesise and test
buildSteps.detail: Make the most promising candidates in a laboratory — increasingly with robotic platforms — and measure their real properties.

buildSteps.title: Retrain and iterate
buildSteps.detail: Feed the new experimental results back into the models to improve their accuracy and guide the next round of predictions.

buildSteps.title: Scale up
buildSteps.detail: Optimise synthesis and processing parameters so the material can be produced reliably at commercial quantities.

prerequisites.why: provides the large, consistent datasets needed to train machine learning models when experimental data is scarce.
many public and private databases exist, but they use different formats and quality standards, which limits how easily they can be combined.

prerequisites.tech: Machine learning algorithms for structured data
prerequisites.why: graph neural networks and related methods can learn from crystal structures and compositions directly.
some systems can synthesise and test materials automatically, but they are not yet widespread or fully general.
training large models and running high-throughput simulations requires substantial computing resources, often using GPUs.

pathway.milestone: machine learning models predict properties and guide experimental choices in academic and commercial materials informatics
pathway.unlocks: faster screening of candidates and reduced trial-and-error in early-stage research.

pathway.milestone: closed-loop autonomous laboratories that design, synthesise, characterise and retrain with minimal human intervention
pathway.unlocks: continuous discovery cycles running day and night.

pathway.milestone: AI integrated with process scale-up, predicting manufacturing parameters and quality
pathway.unlocks: faster transition from a promising material to a manufacturable product.

pathway.milestone: routine discovery of materials with targeted, unprecedented properties such as better superconductors, catalysts or battery components
pathway.unlocks: accelerated innovation across energy, electronics and healthcare.
